name: IL-15
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+20 partisan lean makes a Democratic win structurally unlikely
Incumbent Mary Miller holds a roughly 17-to-1 cash-on-hand advantage over Jennifer Todd
Prediction markets price a Republican hold near 95 percent
No public polls or expert ratings cover the race; the national environment is the main Democratic offset
model.rationale: An R+20 incumbent seat, Miller's dominant fundraising edge, and market pricing near 95 percent Republican all point the same way, and no polling or rating evidence suggests the challenger has closed the gap.
model.watch: Only a major scandal involving Miller or a decisive national Democratic wave could put this seat in play.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Illinois' 15th District is among the most Republican-leaning seats in the state, with a partisan lean of roughly twenty points toward the GOP. Representative Mary Miller seeks another term as the incumbent, while Democrat Jennifer Todd enters as a first-time challenger with modest resources. No public polls or expert ratings track the race, so the picture rests on district fundamentals, fundraising, and market pricing.

Miller holds a decisive financial edge, having raised about 1.8 million dollars to Todd's roughly 200,000, and enters the final stretch with more than 900,000 dollars on hand. Prediction markets give Republicans about a 95 percent chance of holding the seat. A favorable national environment for Democrats could shave a few points off the Republican margin, but nothing in the available evidence suggests the race is genuinely competitive. A Republican victory is the clear expectation.
